exercises.title: Liquidity after haircuts
exercises.intro: Liquidity counts assets after haircuts and after cash to close (F-CORE-24, CORE-BOR-11). Then compare it with the post-closing requirement (F-CORE-25, CORE-BOR-12).

calculator.task: Work out Dana Reyes's adjusted liquidity for Maple Run. The requirement is max(10% × $340,000 = $34,000; 6 × $340,000 × 10.25% ÷ 12 = $17,425) = $34,000. Does she pass, and by how much? Then set the HELOC to $0: does the result change?

exercises.title: Does it count toward the tier?
exercises.intro: Experience counts projects completed in the last 36 months with at least 20% ownership (F-CORE-27, CORE-BOR-15). Sort each project.

items.text: Dana Reyes: one of six flips sold in the last 36 months, owned 50-100%
items.why: Sold inside 36 months with at least 20% ownership. All six count, so Dana's count is 6: Tier 2 (CORE-BOR-16).

items.text: Dana Reyes: a flip sold 14 months ago where she owned 15%
Marcus Hale: 40-unit property, owned 50%, held and operated since 2021
items.why: A property held and operated 12 months or more counts as completed (CORE-BOR-18), as rental experience.

items.text: Marcus Hale: 24-unit property, owned 35%, sold in 2025
items.why: Sold inside 36 months at 35% ownership. With the 40-unit, Marcus counts 2: Tier 1.

items.text: A flip sold in the last 36 months where the guarantor owned exactly 20%
items.why: Exactly 20% meets the test (CORE-BOR-15; quiz A10).

items.text: A flip sold 38 months ago, owned 100%
items.why: 38 months is outside the 36-month lookback. Exactly 36 months would count (D-CONV-03).

items.text: A flip renovated and refinanced into a rental 10 months ago, owned 25%
items.why: A refinance into a term rental loan is a completion (CORE-BOR-15; quiz B10).

items.text: A rental owned 30%, held and operated for exactly 12 months in the lookback
items.why: A hold of exactly 12 months counts, as rental experience (CORE-BOR-18).

items.text: Priya Nand: 12 years as a property manager, with no ownership
items.why: Managing can help the MF-GEN-07 gate, but the tier counts only ownership (F-CORE-27).

exercises.title: Tier, caps and approver
exercises.intro: Exposure is the new commitment plus every open commitment to the sponsor and affiliates (F-CORE-29). Test it against the tier caps, then name the approver (CORE-CONC-01, CORE-AUTH-01).

start.q: Is sponsor exposure above the tier's dollar cap? (Tier 0 $1,000,000; Tier 1 $3,000,000; Tier 2 $7,500,000; Tier 3 $15,000,000)

loans.q: Counting the new loan, are open loans above the tier's loan cap? (Tier 0: 2; Tier 1: 5; Tier 2: 10; Tier 3: 20)

size.q: Is the loan over $2,000,000, or exposure over $5,000,000?

su.q: Is it Residential, with the loan up to $500,000, exposure up to $1,000,000 and no exceptions?

end_conc.result: Committee only: a concentration cap is breached.
end_conc.explain: Above either the dollar cap or the loan cap, only committee can approve (CORE-CONC-01, CORE-AUTH-01).

end_committee.explain: Committee approves loans above $2,000,000 or exposure above $5,000,000 (CORE-AUTH-01).

end_co.explain: A credit officer approves up to a $2,000,000 loan and $5,000,000 exposure, with one exception at most (CORE-AUTH-01).

end_su.explain: A senior underwriter with the family certificate approves Residential loans up to $500,000 and $1,000,000 exposure, with no exceptions (CORE-AUTH-01).
